notes: Historical figures are annual, from Cisco consolidated statements in the FY2025 Form 10-K (all $ amounts in full USD units; original disclosure in $ millions). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/858877/000085887725000111/csco-20250726.htm))

EBIT is proxied by Cisco GAAP operating income; D&A uses the cash flow line item 'Depreciation, amortization, and other' (may include other non-cash add-backs beyond pure depreciation/amortization). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/858877/000085887725000111/csco-20250726.htm))

Net working capital (NWC) definition used: (Total current assets - cash and cash equivalents - current investments) - (Total current liabilities - short-term debt). Negative NWC reflects deferred revenue-heavy working capital. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/858877/000085887725000111/csco-20250726.htm))

Tax rate used in DCF is normalized to FY2024 effective tax rate (0.156) rather than FY2025 (0.083) due to a one-time tax benefit. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/858877/000085887725000111/csco-20250726.htm))

WACC derived using: risk-free from FRED DGS10 (4.25% on 2026-03-19 observation), beta from Yahoo Finance (0.87), cost of debt from FY2025 interest expense / average total debt, and capital structure weights using tool market cap and total debt; resulting WACC = 0.0825. ([fred.stlouisfed.org](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/dGs10))

NOL balance is total federal + state + foreign NOL carryforwards before valuation allowance (2.917B USD). NOL utilization % is not disclosed in the filings, so set to null. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/858877/000085887725000111/csco-20250726.htm))

catalysts: Upside from continued AI infrastructure demand translating into product growth and improved operating leverage in subsequent quarters.
Quarterly execution/cost discipline that sustains operating margin at or above guidance ranges.
Potential portfolio and acquisition-related synergies (including AI/software contributions) supporting sustained earnings power.
company_overview: Cisco designs and sells networking, security, collaboration, and observability technologies that help customers securely run and manage enterprise and service-provider infrastructure. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/858877/000085887724000017/csco-20240727.htm))

Revenue is supported by both products and services, with services including recurring-type offerings and support-related streams. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/858877/000085887725000111/csco-20250726.htm))

Cisco remains active on AI-related product innovation and acquisitions to broaden its portfolio. ([investor.cisco.com](https://investor.cisco.com/news/news-details/2026/CISCO-REPORTS-SECOND-QUARTER-EARNINGS/default.aspx))
current_context: In Q2 FY2026 (ended Jan. 24, 2026), Cisco reported revenue of $15.3B (+10% y/y) and GAAP EPS of $0.80; management highlighted operating margin above the high end of guidance. ([investor.cisco.com](https://investor.cisco.com/news/news-details/2026/CISCO-REPORTS-SECOND-QUARTER-EARNINGS/default.aspx))

FY2026 guidance (full year) calls for revenue of $61.2B to $61.7B; Cisco also guided FY2026 effective tax provision rate of ~16% (GAAP) and ~19% (non-GAAP). ([investor.cisco.com](https://investor.cisco.com/news/news-details/2026/CISCO-REPORTS-SECOND-QUARTER-EARNINGS/default.aspx))

Q3 FY2026 guidance includes revenue of $15.4B to $15.6B (with non-GAAP operating margin guidance provided in the press release). ([investor.cisco.com](https://investor.cisco.com/news/news-details/2026/CISCO-REPORTS-SECOND-QUARTER-EARNINGS/default.aspx))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth is anchored to the near-term FY2026 guidance range and then normalizes to a mature, low-to-mid single digit growth profile through FY2030.
EBIT margin is modeled to recover gradually from FY2025 (reflecting profitability normalization after prior-year charges) toward a ~0.218 terminal EBIT margin.
Capital intensity is kept stable via capex at ~1.5% of sales, consistent with Cisco’s historical capex-to-sales range.
Working-capital intensity remains negative (NWC as a percent of sales below zero), consistent with Cisco’s business model with deferred revenue effects.
key_risks: Macro/IT-spend volatility and timing-driven revenue recognition (particularly for large complex deals) affecting growth.
Margin pressure from mix shifts, tariffs, and ongoing amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets.
Tax volatility and uncertainty around NOL utilization could affect realized cash taxes vs. modeled rates.

presentation.subtitle: Cisco (CSCO) DCF + Comps Valuation Inputs (Base Case)
valuation_summary: DCF base case uses normalized tax rate (0.156), WACC of ~0.0825, and terminal growth of 0.025 under a Gordon growth terminal value framework.
The modeled near-term growth profile is consistent with FY2026 revenue guidance ($61.2B to $61.7B), helping anchor the early-year cash flow estimates.
Comps are provided as a directional cross-check; EV/NTM revenue and EV/NTM EBITDA were not populated due to NTM-specific EV multiple availability in accessible sources.
